batches.prompt: Create a precise 3-column by 2-row grid of SIX independent square photographic images, edge-to-edge equal panels, total canvas 1536x1024. No gutters, borders, captions, numbers, labels or typography. These are potential small thumbnails for a British vegetable gardening book. Every panel must be genuinely photographic in appearance, plausible real UK garden details, natural plant variation and soft daylight, restrained colour, clarity at small thumbnail size. Keep each principal subject within its own central 80%, no objects crossing panels. Reference 1 is only the existing photographic tone; reference 2 contains botanical illustrations ONLY for subject shape and symptom morphology, do NOT copy its illustrated style or pale cutout backgrounds. Reference 3 is John's real allotment: use real garden texture and context, no invented formal garden. Shallow backgrounds, crisp subject detail, no heavy processing or shiny CGI. ROW-MAJOR subjects: TOP LEFT (05) black bean aphids: close view of a broad bean growing tip with a colony of tiny matte black aphids clustered around tender stem and unfolding leaves; recognisable grey-green broad bean oval leaves, naturally irregular positions. TOP CENTRE (06) large white butterfly caterpillar: one realistic yellow-green caterpillar patterned black with fine hairs, resting along a cabbage leaf vein beside irregular chewed holes, anatomical realism, modest size against leaf. TOP RIGHT (07) flea beetle feeding damage: close view of a young radish leaf peppered with naturally varied small rounded shot-holes and shallow pale feeding pits, tiny black beetle optional but only realistically tiny; no regular polka dot pattern. BOTTOM LEFT (08) cabbage whitefly: underside of a blue-green cabbage leaf, tiny white roof-winged whiteflies scattered irregularly along veins; each is millimetres long, some subtle grey wing spots, no moth-sized insects. BOTTOM CENTRE (09) leek rust: close-up of a curved blue-green leek blade bearing elongated orange raised pustules of varying age, remaining foliage green, real dusty leaf texture. BOTTOM RIGHT (10) blossom-end rot: one ripening red tomato hanging naturally from its calyx, seen obliquely from below so a dark brown sunken leathery patch at the bottom blossom scar is unmistakable and opposite the stem; no wound near calyx, natural tomato leaves blurred behind.

BOTTOM RIGHT (16) cabbage white butterfly: one small white butterfly perched naturally on edge of a cabbage leaf, wings partially folded, off-white wings with soft yellow-green underside and subtle grey speckling, dark forewing tip just visible, slim body with six slender legs and two clubbed antennae; realistic UK garden macro, no extra wings or fused insects.

method: Two grids of six generated photographic studies; reference artwork used only for morphology, original camera material for garden context. All new artwork is generated, not camera evidence.
